nodes.name: Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement:
Suppose $n\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, \hbox{$p,\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$} with $p\!>\!2$, 
$J\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)$, $C\!\in\!L^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)$,
and $u\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\mathbb{C}^n)$ are such~that 
\begin{equation} u(0)=0, \qquad
J(z)^2=-\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, ~~
u_s(z)+J(z)u_t(z)+C(z)u(z)=0 ~~\forall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation}
Then, there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, 
$\Phi\!\in\!L_1^p(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R)$, and 
a $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic map $\sigma\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ such~that 
\begin{equation} \sigma(0)=0, \qquad
J(z)\Phi(z)=\Phi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n},~~u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z)
~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.\end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 4.1
nodes.statement:
If $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$
compatible with~$J$,  there exists a continuous function 
\hbox{$\hbar_{J,g}\!:X\!\times\!\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} with the following property. 
If \hbox{$u\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a $J$-holomorphic map such that 
$$u(B_R)\subset B_r^g(x) \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad
E_g(u)<\hbar_{J,g}(x,r)$$
for some $x\!\in\!X$ and $r\!\in\!\mathbb R$, then
\begin{equation} \big|\textnormal{d}_0u\big|_g^2<\frac{16}{\pi R^2} E_g(u)\,.\end{equation}

nodes.name: Corollary 3.4
nodes.statement:
Suppose $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a Riemann surface,
and $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a  $J$-holomorphic map.
If $u$ is not constant on every connected component of~$\Sigma$, then the~subset 
$$u^{-1}\big(\{u(z)\!:\,z\!\in\!\Sigma,~\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0\}\big)\subset\Sigma$$
is discrete. If in addition $x\!\in\!X$, the subset $u^{-1}(x)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ 
is also discrete.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.8
nodes.statement:
Let $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold and $g$ be a Riemannian metric on~$X$.
If $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ and $u\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a continuous map such that 
$u|_{B_R^*}$ is a $J$-holomorphic map and $E_g(u;B_R^*)\!<\!\infty$, 
then $u$ is smooth and $J$-holomorphic on~$B_R$.

nodes.name: Corollary 4.2
nodes.statement:
If $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$, 
then there exists $\hbar_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such that 
$E_g(u)\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$ for every non-constant $J$-holomorphic map
$u\!:S^2\!\longrightarrow\!X$.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.12
nodes.statement:
If $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$ compatible with~$J$, 
there exists a continuous function $C_{g,J}\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$
with the following property.
If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact Riemann surface with boundary,
\hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a $J$-holomorphic map, 
$x\!\in\!X$, and $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ are such that 
$u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$, then 
\begin{equation} E_g(u)\ge \big(\textnormal{ord}_xu\big)\frac{\pi\delta^2}{{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}}\,.\end{equation}
If $\omega(\cdot,\cdot)\equiv\!g(J\cdot,\cdot)$ is a symplectic form on~$X$, 
then the above fraction can be replaced by the product $\pi\delta^2\textnormal{e}^{-C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2}$.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.1
nodes.statement:
Let $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold
and $u\!:B_R^*\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a $J$-holomorphic map.
If the energy $E_g(u)$ of~$u$, with respect to any metric~$g$ on~$X$, 
is finite, then $u$ extends to a $J$-holomorphic map 
$\widetilde{u}\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$.

nodes.name: Corollary 4.17
nodes.statement:
If $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$, 
there exist $\hbar_{J,g},C_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property.
If $u\!:[-R,R]\!\times\!S^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a \hbox{$J$-holomorphic} map such that 
$E_g(u)\!<\!\hbar_{J,g}$, then 
\begin{alignat*}{2}
E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1\big) &\le C_{J,g}\textnormal{e}^{-T}E_g(u)
&\qquad&\forall~T\ge1,\\
\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u([-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1)\big)
&\le C_{J,g}\textnormal{e}^{-T/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)} &\quad&\forall~T\ge2\,.
\end{alignat*}

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2, Lemma 5.4: - <<<
nodes.statement:
Suppose $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$
and \hbox{$u_i\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps converging
uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$
to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such that the limit
\begin{equation}\mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})\end{equation}
exists and is nonzero. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=*]

\item The limit $\mathfrak m(\delta)\equiv\lim\limits_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})$ 
exists and is a continuous, non-decreasing function of~$\delta$.

\item For every sequence $z_i\!\in\!B_1$ converging to~0,
$\lim\limits_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i))\!=\!\mathfrak m(\delta)$.

\item For every sequence $z_i\!\in\!B_1$ converging to~0,
$\mu\!\in\!(0,\mathfrak m)$, and $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large,
there exists a unique $\delta_i(\mu)\!\in\!(0,1\!-\!|z_i|)$ such that 
$E_g(u_i;B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\!=\!\mu$.
Furthermore, 
\begin{equation}
\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{R\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big)
=\mathfrak m\!-\!\mu.\end{equation}

\end{enumerate}

If $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$,
then there exists a function $N\!:\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!{\mathbb Z}$ with the following property.
If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is compact Riemann surface, $S_0\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is a finite subset,
 and $u_i\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps 
from open subsets of~$\Sigma$ with 
\begin{equation}U_i\subset U_{i+1}, \qquad \Sigma\!-\!S_0=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}\!U_i,
\quad\hbox{and}\quad E\!\equiv\!\liminf_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)<\infty,\end{equation}
then there exist a subset $S\!\subset\!\Sigma$ with $|S|\!\le\!N(E)\!+\!|S_0|$ 
and a subsequence of $u_i$ converging  uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology 
on compact subsets of $\Sigma\!-\!S$
to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.5
nodes.statement:
Let $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$
and $u_i\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps converging
uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$
to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$. If the limit
\begin{equation}\mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})\end{equation}

exists and is nonzero, then there exist
\begin{enumerate}[ref=\arabic*,label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=*]

\item a nodal Riemann surface $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ consisting of $B_1$ with 
a tree of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ attached at $0\!\in\!B_1$,

\item a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$,
 
\item a subsequence of $\{u_i\}$ still denoted by $\{u_i\}$, and

\item a biholomorphic map $\psi_i\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!B_{1/2}$, 
where $U_i\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ is an open subset,  

\end{enumerate}
such that 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(psi_it\alph*),leftmargin=*]

\item $E_g(u_{\infty};\Sigma_{\infty}\!-\!B_1)=\mathfrak m$, 
$U_i\!\subset\!U_{i+1}$, and $\mathbb{C}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}U_i$,

\item $u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i$ converges to~$u_{\infty}$ uniformly 
in the $C^{\infty}$-topology  on compact subsets of the complement of the nodes 
$\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_k^*$  in the sphere~$\mathbb{P}_0^1$ attached at $0\!\in\!B_1$,

\item  if $u_{\infty}|_{\mathbb{P}^1_0}$ is constant, 
$\mathbb{P}^1_0$ contains at least three nodes of~$\Sigma_{\infty}$;

\item (psi_it) applies with $B_1$, $(\{u_i\},0)$,  and~$\mathfrak m$
replaced by  a neighborhood of~$w_r^*$ in~$\mathbb{C}$, $(\{u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i\},w_r^*)$, and 
\begin{equation}\mathfrak m_r'\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}
E_g\big(u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i;B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big),\end{equation}
respectively, for each $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$.

\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement:
Let $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold with Riemannian metric~$g$,
$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a compact Riemann surface, and $u_i\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a sequence
of non-constant $J$-holomorphic maps.
If $\liminf E_g(u_i)\!<\!\infty$, then the sequence $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u_i)$ contains
a subsequence
converging to some stable $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$
in the sense of Definition~1.1.
